chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shazaan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-Abd al-Salih (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'My mother breast-fed a girl with my milk.' He said, 'She is your sister from breast-feeding.' I said, 'So would it be permissible for my brother from my mother, who did not breast-feed her with his milk — meaning not with this pregnancy, but with another pregnancy?' He said, 'And the stallion (father) is one?' I said, 'Yes, she is my sister of my father and my mother.' He said, 'The milk is of the stallion (father). Your father has become her father, and your mother, her mother.'
ai.seo_question: How does breast-feeding create sibling relationships in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the mechanism of 'radha' (breast-feeding) by establishing that the source of the milk (the 'fahl' or male equivalent in lineage) determines the kinship ties, effectively making the nursing woman's husband the father of the nursed child. It specifically addresses the nuance that the milk's origin in a specific pregnancy does not limit the legal effect, reinforcing the principle that the act of nursing creates a permanent mahram relationship akin to biological parenthood. This ruling is foundational in Shia fiqh for determining marriage prohibitions and inheritance rights through fosterage.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, from Safwan Bin Yahya, 
(It has been narrated) from Al-Abd Al-Salih<sup>asws</sup> (7<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>), said,

‘I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘My mother breast-fed a girl with my milk’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘She is your sister from the breast-feeding’. So I said, ‘So would it be Permissible for my brother from my mother who did not breast-feed from his milk, meaning not with this pregnancy, but with another pregnancy’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And the stallion (father) is one?’ I said, ‘Yes, she is my sister of my father and my mother’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The milk is of the stallion (father). Your father has become her father, and your mother, as her mother’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn ‘Isma’il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan ibn Yahya who has said the following: “This is concerning my question before Allah’s virtuous servant, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of my mother who has breastfed a girl along with me. He (the Imam) said, ‘She is your sister of breastfeeding.’ I then asked if she is lawful for my brother from my mother’s side whom she has not breastfed with his milk, that is not from this pregnancy but from another pregnancy. He (the Imam) asked, ‘Is the ‘impregnating agent’ (husband) one?’ I replied, ‘Yes, she is my sister from my parents.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Because of the milk of “impregnating agent” your father has become her father and your mother her mother.’”
